kicker: An unofficial port, from its source

scenes.headline: A game engine in a browser tab
scenes.sub: Reading an unofficial port from its own page source
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Brindle! Today, what the page source of an unofficial browser port of a big game shows.

scenes.text: Before the tab asks for the engine, the page checks six things, then picks one build by its hash and streams the game as you play.
scenes.mark: picks one build by its hash
scenes.say: The page checks six things first. Then it picks one engine build by its hash, and streams the game as you play.

scenes.title: What must be true before the engine loads

steps.say: First the page must be secure and isolated, or browsers will not share memory between threads.
Shared memory lets the renderer, the job workers and the loader talk without copying.
A game heap wants sixty four bit memory. Safari lacks it, so phones get a separate build.
Then a graphics adapter must exist. The renderer is built on the new web graphics API.
Only then is a build picked by hash, and the game's archives start to stream.

scenes.label: of engine to download before any game data
scenes.note: compressed, for the bundle the page embeds
scenes.say: The engine alone is about fifty nine megabytes compressed, before a single game archive moves.

scenes.title: How the loading bar is weighted
scenes.say: The bar is weighted, not timed. The engine download is forty percent of it, whatever the clock says.

scenes.text: A browser port is mostly plumbing: checks, caches and workarounds, each one dated by its author.
scenes.say: A port like this is mostly plumbing. Checks, caches and workarounds, each one dated by the person who wrote it.
Six checks, a build chosen by hash, and no licence anywhere in the page.
